title.en: Explain channels of distribution and physical distribution

say.en: Before an advertisement is ever shown, the firm must decide what exactly it sells, at what price, and through which shops. In this lesson: Explain branding, packaging and labelling.
Explain the factors affecting price.
Explain channels of distribution and physical distribution.

body.en: A brand is a name, term, sign, symbol or design that identifies a seller's products; a registered brand is a trademark. *Branding* helps the firm differentiate its product, advertise it and charge a premium, and helps consumers identify quality. Packaging is designing and producing the container or wrapper: it protects the product, aids identification and convenience, and promotes it. Labelling provides information on the package: name, contents, quantity, price (MRP), date of manufacture and expiry, maker's details and instructions; some of this is required by law.

body.en: A channel of distribution is the route by which goods move from producer to consumer. Direct channel (zero level): producer → consumer (door-to-door, company outlets, online). Indirect *channels*: one level (producer → retailer → consumer), two level (producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer) and three level (producer → agent → wholesaler → retailer → consumer). The choice depends on the product (perishable or technical goods need short channels), the market (size and spread), the company (its resources and control) and the environment. Physical distribution covers order processing, transportation, warehousing and inventory control.

say.en: A channel of distribution is the route by which goods move from producer to consumer. Direct channel zero level: producer gives consumer (door-to-door, company outlets, online). Indirect channels: one level (producer gives retailer gives consumer), two level (producer gives wholesaler gives retailer gives consumer) and three level (producer gives agent gives wholesaler gives retailer gives consumer). The choice depends on the product (perishable or technical goods need short channels), the market size and spread, the company (its resources and control) and the environment. Physical distribution covers order processing, transportation, warehousing and inventory control. Zero level: direct.
One, two, three level: indirect.
Choice: product, market, company, environment.
Physical distribution: orders, transport, storage, inventory.

problem.en: Fixed cost ₹1,20,000; variable cost ₹40 a unit; 3,000 units; markup 25%. Find the cost-plus price.

narration.en: Fixed cost ₹1,20,000; variable cost ₹40 a unit; 3,000 units; markup 25%. Find the cost-plus price.

say.en: Fixed cost 1,20,000 rupees; variable cost 40 rupees a unit; 3,000 units; markup 25 percent. Find the cost-plus price.
Fixed cost per unit equals 1,20,000 divided by 3,000 equals 40 rupees.
Total cost per unit equals 40 plus 40 equals 80 rupees.
Price equals 80 times 1.25 equals 100 rupees.
Profit per unit equals 20 rupees.
So the answer is 100 rupees per unit.
